annotation.title_clean: General Understanding on AI and Copyright in Japan - Overview
annotation.title_en: General Understanding on AI and Copyright in Japan - Overview
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Japan Copyright Office, Agency for Cultural Affairs (Legal Subcommittee, Copyright Subdivision, Cultural Council)
annotation.summary_en: Overview of the Japanese Agency for Cultural Affairs' non-binding interpretation of how the existing Copyright Act applies to generative AI, covering training (Article 30-4), infringement at generation/use stage, and copyrightability of AI outputs. It favours applying current law and fostering stakeholder dialogue.
key_provisions_or_claims: Article 30-4 generally permits use of works for AI training without permission when for non-enjoyment purposes
Article 30-4 does not apply where enjoyment purpose exists, e.g., fine-tuning to reproduce specific works or RAG outputting expression
Exception does not apply if it unreasonably prejudices copyright holders' interests, e.g., available data-analysis licences
Infringement of AI outputs is judged by similarity and dependence, as for ordinary infringement
Document is not legally binding; encourages communication among creators, developers and users
